To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Δ 9-tetrahdrocannabinol (Δ 9- THC ) enhances the excitatory effect on cortical unit potentials of iontophorectically administered 2-phenyl ethylamine (PE A), increases the recovery of labeled PEA from brain after intraventricular injection of labeled PEA, induces excitement in mice pretrea ted with reserpine and enhances the excitement induced by PEA in mice pretreated wit Δ 9-THC.
Δ 9-THC increases the recovery of labeled PEA from brain and enhances the excitatory effect iontophoretically applied PEA on cortical units in rabbits.

Δ 9-THC enhances the recovery of labeled phenylethylamine from rabbit brain, increases the excitatory effects of iontophorectic phenylethylamines on cortical unit potentials in rabbits, and induces excitement in reserpinized or pargyline-treated mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible role of 2 phenylethylamine as one of the adrenoergotropic modulators in the action of delta 2 -tetrahydro cannabinol ( Δ 2 -THC).
the possible role of 2-(2-phenylethy)amine (PEA), a monoamine amide, in the mode of the action of the major psychoactive constituent of marihuana, Δ 9-tetrahdrocannabinol (Δ 9 -THO).
the role of endogenous phenylethylamine and the possible interaction between this amine and Δ 9 -tetracydrocannabinol (Δ 9 -THCl).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Δ 9- THC inhibits the disposition and/or metabolism of PEA and that the latter, as an adrenergic modulator, may play a role, at least partially, in the euphoric effect of Δ 9-THC.
Δ 9 THC increases the excitatory effect (i.e., ergotropic) of PEA.
Δ 9 THC inhibits the disposition and metabolism of PEA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Δ 9-THC increases the concentration of PEA in brain by inhibiting its metabolism and/or excretion, and this increase may contribute to the euphoriant action of Δ 9- THC.
the Δ 9 -Tetrahydrocannibinol (Δ 9 -TH) inhibits the disposition (metabolism) of 2-Phenylethylamine.
PEA is a neuromodulator that is involved in the euphoric effects of Δ 9 -Tetrahydrocannibinol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PEA, which is a precursor of phenylethanolamines, may be involved in the euphoric effects of cannabis.
PEA, a naturally occurring substance, may be a major factor in the euphoric and other effects of cannabis.
Δ9-THC is not only a cannabinoid receptor agonist, but also an inhibitor of the metabolism and reuptake of 2-PEA, an adrenergic neurotransmitter.
